items.title: Flagship Rural Development Schemes
items.body:
**In one line** — A bundle of central schemes gives rural households wage work, roads, houses and livelihoods, delivered through the panchayat system.

**Why it is asked** — Scheme-to-purpose matching, launch years and the administering ministry are near-certain one-mark questions.

## The story

Rural development is a **multi-dimensional effort** to raise rural incomes and living standards through **infrastructure, credit, wage and self-employment, housing, sanitation and food security**. Most schemes are run by the **Ministry of Rural Development** and delivered through the three-tier **Panchayati Raj** system (73rd Amendment, 1992).

| Scheme | Year | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| MGNREGA | 2005 | Legal guarantee of 100 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household |
| PMGSY | 2000 | All-weather roads to unconnected habitations |
| PMAY-Gramin | 2016 | Pucca houses (replaced Indira Awaas Yojana) |
| DAY-NRLM (Aajeevika) | 2011 | Women SHG-based livelihoods |
| DDU-GKY | 2014 | Placement-linked skilling of rural youth |
| SAGY | 2014 | MPs adopt and develop model villages via convergence |

- **IRDP (1978-80)** was the pioneering self-employment anti-poverty programme, later folded into SGSY and then NRLM.
- Schemes **converge**: a PMAY-G house uses an SBM toilet and MGNREGA labour.

## Terms explained

- **Pucca house** — a permanent house with solid walls and roof (vs a kutcha mud/thatch house).
- **SHG (Self-Help Group)** — a small savings-and-credit group, usually of women.
- **Convergence** — two or more schemes combining funds/efforts on the same beneficiary.

**Don't confuse** — **MGNREGA** guarantees *wage* work (100 days); **DAY-NRLM** builds *self*-employment through SHGs. **SAGY has no separate fund** — the MP works by converging existing schemes.

**Remember it** — Rural 'MPPDDS' = MGNREGA, PMGSY, PMAY-G, DAY-NRLM, DDU-GKY, SAGY.

**TL;DR**

- MGNREGA (2005): 100 guaranteed wage days, one-third women.
- PMGSY (2000) roads; PMAY-G (2016) houses; DAY-NRLM (2011) SHGs; DDU-GKY (2014) skilling; SAGY (2014) model villages.
- IRDP (1978-80) was the early self-employment scheme; all run via Panchayati Raj under the Ministry of Rural Development.
keyPoints: MGNREGA (2005) guarantees 100 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household, with one-third women.
PMGSY (2000) builds all-weather rural roads; PMAY-Gramin (2016) provides pucca houses, replacing Indira Awaas Yojana.
DAY-NRLM/Aajeevika (2011) mobilises rural women into SHGs; DDU-GKY (2014) gives placement-linked skilling.
SAGY (2014) has MPs adopt Gram Panchayats and develop them through convergence, with no separate fund.
IRDP (1978-80) was the early self-employment anti-poverty scheme, later merged into SGSY then NRLM.
items.mnemonic: Rural 'MPPDDS' = MGNREGA, PMGSY, PMAY-G, DAY-NRLM, DDU-GKY, SAGY.
items.source: Ministry of Rural Development / PIB — rural development schemes

items.title: Urban Development Missions (2015 onwards)
items.body:
**In one line** — From 2015 three big urban missions — Smart Cities, AMRUT and PMAY-Urban — took over the job of modernising India's cities.

**Why it is asked** — City counts (100 vs 500), the four PMAY-U verticals and the administering ministry (MoHUA) are standard facts.

## The story

After the **JNNURM (2005)** reform mission wound down, the government launched a cluster of urban missions in **2015** under the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**:

| Mission | Coverage | Thrust |
|---|---|---|
| Smart Cities Mission | 100 cities | Area-based development + a pan-city smart solution, run through an SPV |
| AMRUT | 500 cities/towns (1 lakh+) | Water supply, sewerage, drainage, transport, green spaces |
| PMAY-Urban | Urban poor | 'Housing for All' — four verticals: ISSR, CLSS, AHP, BLC |

- **HRIDAY (2015)** funded heritage-city development (Varanasi, Amaravati, Ajmer, Puri).
- **AMRUT 2.0 (2021)** targets universal tap-water and sewerage; **PMAY-U 2.0 (2024)** adds about one crore urban houses.
- **DAY-NULM** covers urban SHGs, self-employment, homeless shelters and street vendors (with **PM SVANidhi**, 2020, for vendor loans).

## Terms explained

- **SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle)** — a dedicated company set up to implement each Smart City's projects.
- **Area-based development** — upgrading one chosen pocket of a city (retrofit/redevelop/greenfield).
- **PMAY-U verticals** — ISSR (in-situ slum redevelopment), CLSS (credit-linked subsidy), AHP (affordable housing in partnership), BLC (beneficiary-led construction).

**Don't confuse** — **Smart Cities = 100 cities**; **AMRUT = 500 towns**. **PMAY-U** (urban, MoHUA) is different from **PMAY-Gramin** (rural, Ministry of Rural Development).

**Remember it** — Urban 'SAPH' = Smart Cities, AMRUT, PMAY-U, HRIDAY (plus NULM for livelihoods).

**TL;DR**

- Smart Cities (100 cities, SPV, area-based + pan-city), AMRUT (500 towns, water first), PMAY-U (4 verticals).
- AMRUT 2.0 (2021), PMAY-U 2.0 (2024, ~1 crore houses), HRIDAY (heritage), DAY-NULM + PM SVANidhi (vendors).
- All under MoHUA; JNNURM (2005) was the predecessor.
keyPoints: Smart Cities Mission (2015) targets 100 cities via area-based + pan-city development through an SPV.
AMRUT (2015) covers 500 towns with water supply as top priority; AMRUT 2.0 (2021) targets universal water/sewerage.
PMAY-Urban has four verticals — ISSR, CLSS, AHP, BLC; PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) adds about 1 crore houses.
HRIDAY (2015) funded heritage-city development; JNNURM (2005) was the predecessor urban-reform mission.
DAY-NULM handles urban livelihoods, shelters and street vendors, complemented by PM SVANidhi (2020).
items.mnemonic: Urban 'SAPH' = Smart Cities, AMRUT, PMAY-U, HRIDAY (+ NULM for livelihoods).
items.source: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs / PIB — urban missions

items.title: Swachh Bharat Mission & Sanitation
items.body:
**In one line** — The Swachh Bharat Mission set out to end open defecation and then to manage waste, treating sanitation as a development and health lever.

**Why it is asked** — The launch date, the ODF declaration year, the two wings and SBM 2.0's focus are repeat facts.

## The story

- The **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)**, launched **2 October 2014**, aimed at an **Open Defecation Free (ODF) India** through mass toilet construction and behaviour change.
- It has **two wings**: **SBM-Gramin** (Ministry of Jal Shakti) and **SBM-Urban** (MoHUA).
- India was declared **ODF in October 2019** (Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary).
- **SBM 2.0 (2021)** shifts to **ODF-Plus** — *sustaining* ODF plus **solid and liquid waste management**, plastic-waste and greywater management.
- It converges with PMAY (every new house gets a toilet) and improves rural health and women's safety and dignity.

## Terms explained

- **ODF (Open Defecation Free)** — a village/town where everyone uses a toilet, with none defecating in the open.
- **ODF-Plus** — the next stage: staying ODF *and* managing solid/liquid waste.
- **Greywater** — used household water (from washing/bathing) that needs safe disposal.

**Don't confuse** — SBM is about **sanitation/toilets**, not drinking water (that is the **Jal Jeevan Mission**) or LPG (**Ujjwala**).

**Remember it** — SBM 1.0 = build toilets (ODF, 2019); SBM 2.0 = keep clean + manage waste (ODF-Plus).

**TL;DR**

- SBM launched 2 Oct 2014; India declared ODF Oct 2019.
- Two wings: SBM-Gramin (Jal Shakti), SBM-Urban (MoHUA).
- SBM 2.0 (2021) = ODF-Plus + solid/liquid/plastic/greywater waste management.
keyPoints: SBM launched 2 October 2014 to make India Open Defecation Free (ODF).
SBM-Gramin is under Ministry of Jal Shakti; SBM-Urban under MoHUA.
India declared ODF in October 2019.
SBM 2.0 (2021) focuses on ODF-Plus — solid/liquid, plastic and greywater waste management.
SBM converges with PMAY so that houses include toilets, aiding health and women's safety.

items.title: Urbanisation — Definition, Trends & Challenges
items.body:
**In one line** — How the Census decides what counts as 'urban', how fast India is urbanising, and the problems that growth brings.

**Why it is asked** — The exact census-town criteria (5,000 / 400 / 75%) and the ~31% urban share are classic data points.

## The story — defining 'urban'

An **urban area** = all **statutory towns** (with a municipality, corporation, notified area or cantonment) **plus census towns** that meet all three criteria:

1. **Population of at least 5,000**
2. **Density of at least 400 persons per sq km**
3. **At least 75% of the male working population in non-agricultural work**

## The story — trends and challenges

- The urban population share was about **31% in Census 2011**, projected to rise toward **~40% by around 2030**.
- Rapid, unplanned urbanisation brings **slums and informal settlements, distress migration, solid-waste and sewage burdens, congestion, and strain on housing and water**.
- The policy response is the mission cluster (Smart Cities, AMRUT, PMAY-U, SBM-U) plus urban-local-body reforms under the **74th Amendment (1992)**.

## Terms explained

- **Statutory town** — a town with a legal urban local body (municipality etc.).
- **Census town** — a settlement that is 'urban' only because it meets the three demographic criteria, without a formal municipality.
- **Distress migration** — people moving to cities out of rural hardship, not choice.

**Don't confuse** — A **statutory town** (has a municipal body) with a **census town** (qualifies only by population/density/occupation). The **74th Amendment** covers *urban* bodies; the **73rd** covers *rural* panchayats.

**Remember it** — Census-town test '5-4-75' = 5,000 people, 400 density, 75% non-farm male workers.

**TL;DR**

- Urban = statutory towns + census towns (5,000 / 400 per sq km / 75% non-agri male workers).
- ~31% urban in 2011, rising toward ~40% by 2030.
- Challenges: slums, migration, waste, congestion, housing; 74th Amendment empowers urban local bodies.
keyPoints: Urban area = statutory towns + census towns meeting population, density and non-agri workforce criteria.
Census-town criteria: population >= 5,000; density >= 400 per sq km; >= 75% male workers in non-agriculture.
Census 2011 urban share was about 31%, projected to rise toward ~40% by 2030.
Challenges: slums, distress migration, solid-waste/sewage load, congestion and housing shortage.
74th Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to urban local bodies (Part IX-A, Twelfth Schedule).

items.title: Rural Credit, Institutions, Land Records & Labour Concepts
items.body:
**In one line** — Who lends to villages, how district credit is planned, the key poverty/labour concepts, and the land-records modernisation drive.

**Why it is asked** — The NABARD 'refinance-only' trap, the Lead Bank/Service Area link, MPL=0, and the DILRMP funding trap are all tested with tricky distractors.

## The story — rural credit institutions

| Institution | Role |
|---|---|
| **NABARD** (1982) | Apex body — it **refinances** banks and pioneered **SHG-Bank Linkage (1992)**, but does **not** lend directly to farmers |
| **RRBs** | Give **direct** credit to rural households (small farmers, artisans) |
| **Land Development Banks** | Give **direct** long-term (mortgage) credit |
| Cooperatives | PACS → DCCB → State Cooperative Bank; **PACS** are the village primary societies |

## The story — credit-planning machinery

- **Lead Bank Scheme (1969)** — each **district is 'adopted' by a lead bank** for intensive credit development.
- **Service Area Approach (1989)** — operates **under the Lead Bank Scheme**, assigning villages to bank branches for planned lending.
- **DRDA (District Rural Development Agency)** — coordinates anti-poverty programmes and monitors fund use at district level.

## The story — labour & poverty concepts

- **Disguised unemployment** — more workers than a job needs, so the **marginal productivity of labour is zero** (typical of family farms).
- **Demographic dividend** — a young workforce lifts growth **only if** backed by skilling, health and jobs.
- **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** — compiled by **OPHI + UNDP**; measures deprivation in **health, education and standard of living**; India also has a **National MPI (NITI Aayog)**.

## The story — land records (DILRMP)

- The **Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP)** works toward **conclusive land titling** by **digitising cadastral (survey) maps** and **transliterating Records of Rights (RoR) into Constitution-recognised languages**, giving each plot a unique ID (**ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar**).
- *Exam trap:* since **1 April 2016 DILRMP is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding** — so a statement calling it a **'Centrally Sponsored (cost-shared) Scheme' is wrong**. The safe hinge-facts are the cadastral-map and RoR-transliteration components.

## Terms explained

- **Refinance** — lending to banks so they can on-lend; NABARD does this, it is not a direct lender.
- **Cadastral map** — an official survey map showing each land parcel's boundaries.
- **Central Sector vs Centrally Sponsored Scheme** — fully central-funded vs cost-shared with states.

**Don't confuse** — **NABARD does not lend directly** (RRBs and Land Development Banks do). And DILRMP is a **Central Sector Scheme (100% central)**, **not** a cost-shared Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

**Remember it** — Direct rural credit = RRB + LDB; NABARD only RE-finances (R for Refinance).

**TL;DR**

- NABARD (1982) refinances (not direct); RRBs/LDBs lend directly; Lead Bank (1969) → Service Area (1989).
- Disguised unemployment = MPL zero; MPI by OPHI + UNDP (National MPI by NITI Aayog); DRDA coordinates districts.
- DILRMP: digitises cadastral maps + transliterates RoR (ULPIN/Bhu-Aadhaar); it is a 100%-central-funded Central Sector Scheme (since 2016).
keyPoints: NABARD (1982) refinances banks and pioneered SHG-Bank Linkage (1992); it does NOT lend directly — RRBs and Land Development Banks give direct rural credit.
Lead Bank Scheme (1969): each district is adopted by a lead bank; Service Area Approach (1989) operates under it.
DRDA coordinates district anti-poverty programmes and monitors fund utilisation.
Disguised unemployment = marginal productivity of labour is zero; demographic dividend needs skilling/health/jobs.
MPI (OPHI + UNDP) measures health, education and living-standard deprivation; India has a National MPI (NITI Aayog).

DILRMP digitises cadastral maps and transliterates RoR to recognised languages (ULPIN/Bhu-Aadhaar); since 2016 it is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding, so calling it a cost-shared 'Centrally Sponsored Scheme' is wrong.
items.mnemonic: Direct rural credit = RRB + LDB; NABARD only RE-finances (R for Refinance).
items.source: NABARD; RBI — Lead Bank Scheme/Service Area Approach; Ministry of Rural Development — DRDA; DoLR — DILRMP; OPHI-UNDP MPI

items.title: Social-Sector Convergence for Inclusive Development
items.body:
**In one line** — Education, nutrition, maternal health and decentralised planning are the social-sector tools that make rural growth inclusive.

**Why it is asked** — RTE/Article 21A, PM POSHAN, the ASHA 'does-not-deliver' point and DPCs (Article 243ZD) are precise discrimination facts.

## The story — education & nutrition

- **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009** — operationalises **Article 21A**; guarantees **free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14**, with **25% EWS seats** in private unaided schools. It is a core human-capital instrument of inclusive growth.
- The **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**, now **PM POSHAN (2021)** — hot cooked meals in government schools that lift **enrolment, retention and child nutrition** together.

## The story — maternal & child health (NRHM)

- **ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)** — a village health volunteer under the **NRHM/NHM (2005)**; she **accompanies women for antenatal care and immunisation and gives nutrition/health counselling**, but **does NOT conduct deliveries herself**.
- **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)** — a **conditional cash-transfer** under NRHM that promotes **institutional (facility) deliveries** to cut maternal and infant mortality.
- *Scope note:* ASHA and JSY are **health-mission** interventions that **converge with** rural development but are run by the health ministry.

## The story — planning & poverty lines

- **District Planning Committees (DPCs)** — mandated by **Article 243ZD**; they **consolidate the plans of panchayats and municipalities** into one district plan.
- **Poverty-line committees:** the **Tendulkar Committee (2009)** and **Rangarajan Committee (2014)** revised India's poverty-line methodology.

## Terms explained

- **Article 21A** — the fundamental right to education (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002).
- **Conditional cash transfer** — money paid only if the beneficiary meets a condition (here, delivering in a facility).
- **EWS** — Economically Weaker Section.

**Don't confuse** — An **ASHA does not conduct deliveries** (she accompanies and counsels); **JSY** pays for *institutional* deliveries. **DPCs** (Article 243ZD) link rural *and* urban plans.

**Remember it** — Convergence 'RAJD' = RTE, ASHA/JSY, PM POSHAN, DPCs.

**TL;DR**

- RTE Act 2009 (Article 21A): free, compulsory schooling 6-14, 25% EWS seats.
- Mid-Day Meal → PM POSHAN (2021): nutrition + retention.
- ASHA (counsels, not deliveries) + JSY (cash for institutional delivery); DPCs (Art 243ZD) merge local plans; Tendulkar (2009)/Rangarajan (2014) on poverty lines.
keyPoints: RTE Act 2009 operationalises Article 21A — free and compulsory education for ages 6-14; a core inclusive-growth/human-capital instrument.
Mid-Day Meal, now PM POSHAN (2021), links school nutrition with enrolment and retention.
ASHA (NRHM/NHM 2005) accompanies women for antenatal care and immunisation and gives nutrition counselling, but does NOT conduct deliveries.
Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a conditional cash transfer under NRHM promoting institutional deliveries.
District Planning Committees (Article 243ZD) consolidate panchayat and municipality plans into a district plan.
Tendulkar (2009) and Rangarajan (2014) committees revised India's poverty-line methodology.
items.mnemonic: Convergence 'RAJD' = RTE, ASHA/JSY, PM POSHAN, DPCs.
items.source: MoE — RTE/PM POSHAN; MoHFW — NRHM (ASHA, JSY); Constitution Art 243ZD; Tendulkar/Rangarajan reports

items.title: Andhra Pradesh — Rural & Urban Development Initiatives
items.body:
**In one line** — Andhra Pradesh pairs a famous women's SHG movement in villages with a dedicated urban-poverty agency in towns.

**Why it is asked** — SERP/Velugu, DWCRA and MEPMA are AP-specific names APPSC prizes, plus the AP smart cities.

## The story — rural AP

- **SERP (Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty)** ran large-scale **women's SHG mobilisation** under **Velugu / Indira Kranthi Patham (IKP)**, building on the earlier **DWCRA** model — a nationally recognised community-driven poverty-reduction approach.
- SHG federations link to **DAY-NRLM** for bank credit and to dairy, livelihood and micro-enterprise work.
- Rural housing, drinking water and roads come through the central schemes (PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan Mission, PMGSY) plus state programmes.

## The story — urban AP

- **MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas)** is the **urban counterpart of SERP**, driving **urban SHGs, DAY-NULM and slum-poor livelihoods**.
- AP cities feature in national missions — **Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Tirupati** under Smart Cities/AMRUT — and the state is developing its capital region **Amaravati**.
- **MeeSeva** citizen-service centres provide e-governance delivery across rural and urban AP.

## Terms explained

- **DWCRA** — Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas, an early AP SHG scheme.
- **Velugu / Indira Kranthi Patham** — AP's flagship SHG-based poverty-reduction programme.
- **MeeSeva** — AP's single-window e-governance service portal ('at your service').

**Don't confuse** — **SERP** is AP's *rural* poverty agency; **MEPMA** is the *urban* one. DWCRA fed into Velugu/IKP, which now links to the national DAY-NRLM.

**Remember it** — 'SERP for villages, MEPMA for municipalities.'

**TL;DR**

- SERP → Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham (from DWCRA): women SHG mobilisation; links to DAY-NRLM.
- MEPMA = AP's urban-poverty agency (urban SHGs, DAY-NULM).
- AP smart cities: Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati; Amaravati capital region; MeeSeva e-governance.
keyPoints: AP's SERP led women's SHG mobilisation under Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham, building on DWCRA.
AP SHG federations link with DAY-NRLM for credit and livelihoods.
MEPMA is AP's urban-poverty agency implementing urban SHGs and DAY-NULM.
Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Tirupati feature in Smart Cities/AMRUT; Amaravati is the capital-region project.
MeeSeva citizen-service e-governance supports service delivery across rural and urban AP.
items.source: Government of Andhra Pradesh — SERP, MEPMA, Municipal Administration & Rural Development

items.title: For Mains — Rural & Urban Development
items.body:
**In one line** — For Mains Paper-IV, rural-urban development is argued as inclusive growth: closing the village-city gap through schemes, decentralised governance and better infrastructure, with Andhra Pradesh's SHG model as the case.

**Why it is asked** — Syllabus clauses M4-6 (inclusive growth — exclusion, poverty alleviation, financial inclusion, PDS, DWCRA) and M4-11 (infrastructure — transport, ICT, energy, smart cities, PPP).

## The dimensions Mains asks

| Dimension | What to write |
|---|---|
| **Why it matters** | ~two-thirds rural, ~31% urban (rising); poverty concentrated rurally; cities as growth engines |
| **Rural instruments** | MGNREGA, PMGSY, PMAY-G, DAY-NRLM, SHG-bank linkage; Panchayati Raj (73rd Amendment) |
| **Urban instruments** | Smart Cities, AMRUT, PMAY-U, SBM; 74th Amendment; ULB finances |
| **Inclusion & convergence** | RTE/PM POSHAN, ASHA/JSY, DPCs (Art 243ZD), financial inclusion (Jan Dhan, DBT), DILRMP titling |
| **Limitations** | Leakage, wage delays, incomplete 3F devolution (functions-funds-functionaries), SPVs vs elected ULBs, jobless growth |
| **Way forward** | Empowered PRIs/ULBs, SHG-market linkage, climate-resilient infrastructure, conclusive land titles |

## Data, committees and schemes to quote

- MGNREGA 100 days; PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) ~1 crore houses; India ODF (2019).
- MPI (OPHI+UNDP) and National MPI (NITI Aayog); Tendulkar (2009)/Rangarajan (2014) poverty lines.
- 73rd & 74th Amendments (1992); DPCs under Article 243ZD; DILRMP (ULPIN/Bhu-Aadhaar).

## The AP angle

- **SERP's Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham** (from **DWCRA**) is a nationally cited women-SHG poverty-reduction model; **MEPMA** mirrors it in towns.
- AP's subsidised-rice PDS legacy (₹2/kg → ₹1/kg) and doorstep ration delivery; smart cities (Vizag, Kakinada, Tirupati); Amaravati land-pooling capital.

## Use in answers

- **Example:** use AP's SERP/Velugu SHG federations to argue that community institutions, not just transfers, drive sustainable poverty reduction.
- **Quote:** inclusive growth is 'growth with jobs and equity' — reaching the last mile.
- **Diagram idea:** two columns (Rural: MGNREGA/PMGSY/PMAY-G/NRLM | Urban: Smart Cities/AMRUT/PMAY-U/NULM) bridged by DPCs and financial inclusion.

**TL;DR** — Frame as inclusive growth bridging the rural-urban divide; quote MGNREGA, the mission cluster, 73rd/74th Amendments, MPI and DILRMP; use AP's SERP/Velugu SHG model and ₹2-rice PDS as the case study.
keyPoints: Mains clauses: M4-6 (inclusive growth) and M4-11 (infrastructure); Paper-IV.
Argue why-it-matters → rural instruments → urban instruments → inclusion/convergence → limits → way forward.
Quote: MGNREGA 100 days, PMAY-U 2.0 ~1 crore, ODF 2019, MPI (OPHI+UNDP), 73rd/74th Amendments, DILRMP.
AP case: SERP/Velugu (from DWCRA) women-SHG model, MEPMA, ₹2-rice PDS, smart cities, Amaravati land pooling.
Way forward: empower PRIs/ULBs (3F devolution), SHG-market linkage, climate-resilient infrastructure, conclusive land titles.
